title: Microsoft Teams: new chat sections for muted and meeting chats
summary: The defaults, rollout targets and absence of tenant controls agree with Microsoft's notice and roadmap. The statements about dragging individual chats and nothing acting on a user's behalf go beyond the documented section behaviour. Licensing should name the general Teams licence requirement while retaining the narrower gap about feature-specific licensing.

claims.claim: Microsoft Teams is introducing new sections for muted and meeting chats.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is introducing two new system chat sections called Muted chats and Meeting chats.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown and not yet published for the new sections.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the licensing notes and the Cost and licensing opening paragraph with: 'Users need a Microsoft Teams licence to use Teams, except when joining meetings anonymously, as stated in Manage Teams licenses. No licence or meter specific to these sections is published at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Replace 'licensing is not yet published' in the cost rationale with 'feature-specific licensing is not yet published'. Replace the licensing open question with 'Will Microsoft publish a licence or meter specific to these sections? Watch the roadmap item and Learn.'
